newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank Scotland buys building society.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank Scotland buys building society.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy one of Britain's biggest building societies, Birmingham Midshires, for 605-630 million pounds ($995 million).
In the middle of the range, the agreed formula implied a price/earnings ratio of about 12 times normalised earnings, Royal Bank said in a statement.
The bank said the acquisition, expected to be completed in the second half of 1998, would have a neutral effect on earnings per share in the first year and be earnings enhancing thereafter.
Royal Bank planned to finance the acquisition without recourse to an equity issue to shareholders.
The bank said the deal would make it Britain's tenth largest mortgage lender managing residential mortgage assets of 12 billion pounds.
"The deal creates many new business opportunities, building on the respective skills and product expertise of each organisation," Royal Bank chief executive George Mathewson said in a statement.
Birmingham Midshires agreed to the deal after a strategic review of its options following the flotation of some of Britain's biggest mutually-held building societies.
"This will be a union of substance and strength, and we are determined to play a key role in the Royal Bank of Scotland," said Birmingham chief executive Mike Jackson.
Birmingham would continue to operate as a separate business within Royal Bank, with existing management in place for at least three years after completion.
The building society said it would close its mortgage processing centre in Bracknell, Berkshire, a move that had already been under consideration.

Birmingham Midshires, with branches concentrated in central, northwest and southwest England, had residential mortgage assets under management of 6.1 billion pounds and retail deposits of 4.5 billion at end 1996. ($ = 0.633 British Pounds)
